study_identification_part.si_3_author_journal_year: Li Sun et al., Journal of Affective Disorders, 2025
study_identification_part.si_4_title: Dissecting heterogeneity in major depressive disorder via normative model-driven subtyping of functional brain networks

nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: Hierarchical Bayesian regression (HBR) was employed using the PCNtoolkit.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: To minimize the impact of site-related variability on subsequent results, hierarchical Bayesian regression (HBR) was employed in the HC cohort to develop a normative model of network degree centrality as a function of age and sex for each brain region
nm2_1_modeling_methods.location: Sun2025.pdf.md: Section 2.3. Capturing individual deviations from normative models

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: Degree centrality (AUC across sparsity thresholds 0.05-0.50) of 96 brain regions (Harvard-Oxford atlas).
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: Degree centrality for each brain region was calculated at every sparsity threshold... with the area under the curve (AUC) across all thresholds defined as a summarized scalar of network indicators... Hierarchical Bayesian regression (HBR) was employed in the HC cohort to develop a normative model of network degree centrality
nm2_2_response_variable.location: Sun2025.pdf.md: Section 2.2. Brain network analysis / Section 2.3. Capturing individual deviations from normative models

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: Age and Sex were used as fixed predictors. Site was used as a grouping factor in the Hierarchical Bayesian Regression.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: In this study, age and sex were mapped onto the degree centrality of brain functional networks... Hierarchical Bayesian regression (HBR) was employed... to estimate site-specific yet interrelated means and variances
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.location: Sun2025.pdf.md: Section 2.3. Capturing individual deviations from normative models
